note: V6-08 (WT W-104, was known gap KG22): the pattern for `2>&1` and `>/dev/null` took quadratic time on a long run of digits: eight times the input took about 55 times as long and 55000 digits passed the 6 s hook budget. A descriptor now starts only at the start of a run of digits. Linear work gives a ratio of about 8, quadratic about 64. Wall-clock case: replayed by the serial `timing` test job only

V6-08 review: a stage whose command word is a variable is read once more for each value, and a nested `g=git;$g $(...)` read it again at every level, so the work doubled at each level (depth 8: 0.4 s, depth 12: 6 s; 0.003 s on the base, which has no such reading). The work is now capped for the whole text, so twice the levels take about as long. Doubling work gives a ratio of 64 for six more levels. Wall-clock case: replayed by the serial `timing` test job only
